 CORAM: HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE NAWNEET KUMAR  PANDEY  ORAL ORDER 5 15-05-2024 Heard the learned counsel for the appellant as well as the learned APP for the State.

2. The matter has been placed before this Court for consideration of the appellant's prayer for bail under Section 374(2) read with section 389(1) of Cr.P.C and suspension of his sentence during the pendency of this appeal.

3. This appeal has been preferred against the judgment dated 05.01.2024 and sentence dated 08.01.2024 and learned Additional Sessions Judge-Ist, Bhagalpur in Sessions Trial No. 767/2013 arising out of Bath P.S. Case No. 15 of 2012 whereby and whereunder the appellant has been convicted for the offences punishable under Sections 376, 363 and 366 (A) of the Indian Penal Code and sentenced for the said offences.

Patna High Court CR. APP (SJ) No.925 of 2024(5)
dt.15-05-2024 4.
While making a prayer for bail after suspension of sentence, the learned senior counsel submits that the age of the victim has not been determined properly.
Her medical examination was done but the medical report could not be brought on record showing her age.
He also submitted that the learned court below did not rely upon the marksheet containing the age of the victim.

Further submission is that, the victim who is allegedly 17 years of age at the time of occurrence had gone Uttam Kumar vs The State Of Bihar on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100534741/
1 with the appellant with her own sweet will.

sentences.text: FIR shows itself that no pressure or force was used against the victim for accompanying the appellant.
He submitted further that in her deposition, the victim herself stated that her father tried to persuade the family members of the appellant for her marriage with the appellant, but they denied.
5. On the other hand, the learned APP for the State has opposed the prayer for suspension of sentence and grant of bail by submitting that as per the FIR, the age of the victim is 17 years.

6. Considering the above-mentioned facts and circumstances especially the fact that the conviction has been made under the POCSO Act but from evidences, it appears prima facie that the age of the victim has not properly been Patna High Court CR.

APP (SJ) No.925 of 2024(5) dt.15-05-2024 established by the prosecution and also considering the fact that there is no likelihood of the appeal being taken up for hearing in near future, this Court is inclined to accept the prayer for bail of the appellant.

Accordingly, let the appellant above-named be enlarged on bail during the pendency of this appeal on furnishing bail bond of Rs. 10,000/- (Ten Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the learned learned Additional Sessions Judge-Ist, Bhagalpur in Sessions Trial No. 767/2013 arising out of Bath P.S. Case No. 15 of 2012.
7.
The execution of sentence shall remain suspended during the pendency of this appeal.
8. During pendency of this appeal, the realization of fine shall remain stayed.

9. List this appeal under appropriate heading in due course.
(Nawneet Kumar Pandey, J) SONALI/-
